On iOS, settings are organized into several major domains within the **Settings** app, ranging from daily customizations to security, accessibility, and enterprise controls. 

Below is a breakdown of what you can change:

---

### 1. Connectivity & Networks
* **Wi-Fi & Bluetooth**: Network connections, Auto-Join, Wi-Fi Assist, Private Wi-Fi Address (MAC randomization), Bluetooth device pairing and device type classification.
* **Cellular / Mobile Data**: 5G/LTE voice and data modes, Data Roaming, Low Data Mode, eSIM management, and per-app cellular data access.
* **Personal Hotspot**: Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/USB tethering, Maximize Compatibility, and Family Sharing access.
* **VPN & Device Management**: VPN connections, enterprise configuration profiles, and Mobile Device Management (MDM) enrollments.
* **Airplane Mode**: Disables cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth radios simultaneously.

---

### 2. Display, Interface & Sound
* **Display & Brightness**: Light/Dark Mode (manual or scheduled), True Tone, Night Shift, Auto-Lock timers, text size & Bold Text, Display Zoom, and Always-On Display (Pro models).
* **Home Screen & Lock Screen**: Wallpaper galleries, lock screen widgets, font styles, icon sizing and tinting (iOS 18+), and whether new apps appear on the Home Screen or App Library only.
* **Sounds & Haptics**: Volume sliders, ringtones, alert tones, keyboard feedback (sound and haptic), Headphone Safety (decibel limits), and silent mode haptics.
* **Action Button & Camera Control** (supported hardware): Reassigning the Action button (Flashlight, Camera, Focus, Shortcut, Translate, etc.) or configuring Camera Control sensitivity.

---

### 3. Privacy, Security & Permissions
* **App Permissions**: Granular, per-app toggles for:
  * Location Services (Never, Ask Next Time, While Using, Always; Precise Location toggle).
  * Photos (None, Limited, Full Access), Camera, Microphone, Contacts, Calendars, and Local Network discovery.
  * App Tracking Transparency (allow/block cross-app tracking).
* **Face ID / Touch ID & Passcode**: Lock screen security, Stolen Device Protection, wallet autofill, and data erase after 10 failed attempts.
* **Safety & Defense Modes**: 
  * **Lockdown Mode**: Extreme security hardening against targeted mercenary spyware.
  * **Safety Check**: Quickly revoke shared access, locations, and app permissions in emergency scenarios.

---

### 4. Notifications, Focus & Screen Time
* **Notifications**: Per-app notification styles (Banner, Alert, Badges, Sounds), Scheduled Summary, and lock screen previews.
* **Focus Modes** (Do Not Disturb, Work, Sleep, Personal, Custom): Filter incoming notifications by person and app, schedule activation, link to specific Lock Screens, and set Focus Filters for system apps (e.g., Mail, Safari tab groups).
* **Screen Time**: Daily app limits, Scheduled Downtime, Communication Limits, Content & Privacy Restrictions (parental controls, explicit content filtering).

---

### 5. System, General & Default Apps
* **Default Apps**: Default web browser, default email client, and default messaging/calling applications.
* **General**: AirDrop (Contacts Only, Everyone for 10 Minutes), AirPlay & Continuity, Picture in Picture auto-start, Date & Time, Language & Region, and Keyboard settings (autocorrect, dictation, text replacements).
* **Storage & Transfer**: iPhone Storage breakdown, Offload Unused Apps, and Reset / Transfer options.
* **Background App Refresh**: Control which apps can fetch data in the background (Wi-Fi, Wi-Fi & Cellular, or Off).

---

### 6. Accessibility
Apple provides deep accessibility customization:
* **Vision**: VoiceOver, Zoom, Display Accommodations (Color Filters, Reduce Transparency, Invert Colors), Motion reduction.
* **Physical & Motor**: AssistiveTouch (virtual on-screen button), Touch Accommodations, Switch Control, Voice Control, and **Back Tap** (double/triple-tap the back of the phone to trigger actions).
* **Hearing & Speech**: Hearing aid pairing, Live Listen, Live Captions, Sound Recognition (alarms, doorbells), and Personal Voice.
* **Assistive Access**: A streamlined, simplified high-contrast UI designed for users with cognitive disabilities.

---

### 7. Battery & Power
* **Low Power Mode**: Limits background sync, reduces display refresh rate (ProMotion), and throttles non-essential animations.
* **Battery Health & Charging**: Maximum capacity view, Optimized Battery Charging, and hard charge limits (e.g., 80% charge ceiling on newer models).

---

### 8. Developer & Enterprise Restrictions
* **Developer Mode**: Required to install custom development builds, connect to Xcode, or use Network Link Conditioner.
* **Supervised Devices & MDM**: Managed corporate/school devices can remotely enforce restrictions, lock down settings, mandate passcodes, push enterprise apps, or block features like AirDrop, iCloud backups, or the App Store.

---

> [!NOTE]
> **For App Developers:** Third-party iOS apps are sandboxed. They cannot programmatically toggle OS-level settings (like toggling Wi-Fi or Bluetooth on/off). They can, however, provide their own custom settings via a Settings Bundle (`Root.plist`) or redirect the user to their app's system settings page using `UIApplication.openSettingsURLString`.

When you create an iOS app, Apple’s sandbox controls what your app can change. You can break this down into **four categories**:

---

### 1. Device Settings Your App Can Change Directly in Code
While your app is running, it can control these hardware and UI behaviors directly:
* **Screen Brightness**: Adjust the screen brightness (`UIScreen.main.brightness`)—commonly used in barcode/ticket scanners to max out brightness automatically.
* **Prevent Screen Sleep (Auto-Lock)**: Keep the screen awake (`UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled = true`) for navigation, workouts, or video apps.
* **Home Screen App Icon**: Let users swap your app’s icon on their Home Screen (`setAlternateIconName`).
* **Flashlight / Torch**: Turn the rear LED flash on/off and control its brightness level via `AVCaptureDevice`.
* **Light / Dark Mode Override**: Force Light or Dark mode inside your app regardless of the phone's system setting (`overrideUserInterfaceStyle`).
* **Audio Behavior**: Choose whether your app’s audio silences other music apps, mixes with them, or plays even when the physical Silent switch is on (`AVAudioSession`).
* **Screen Orientation**: Lock specific screens to Portrait or force them into Landscape (e.g., full-screen video).
* **Join a Wi-Fi Network or VPN**: Prompt the user to automatically join a specific Wi-Fi network (`NEHotspotConfigurationManager`) or configure a VPN profile.

---

### 2. Settings Added to **iOS Settings → [Your App]**
When a user opens the system **Settings** app and scrolls to your app, you control what shows up there:
* **System Permissions**: By adding usage keys to your `Info.plist` and requesting access, iOS automatically generates toggles for **Camera, Microphone, Location, Photos, Bluetooth, Contacts, Calendars, Face ID, Local Network, Notifications, and Background App Refresh**.
* **Preferred Language**: If your app supports multiple languages, iOS adds a per-app language picker automatically.
* **Custom App Settings (`Settings.bundle`)**: You can add custom **Toggles, Sliders, Text Fields, and Dropdowns** directly inside the iOS Settings app (great for server environments, debug flags, or account preferences) that sync directly with `UserDefaults` in your code.
* **Jump to Settings Button**: While your app can't flip a permission toggle itself, you can add a button that jumps the user straight to your app's page in the iOS Settings app (`UIApplication.openSettingsURLString`).

---

### 3. App Configuration & Capabilities (Project Settings)
When configuring the app project itself (`Info.plist`, Entitlements, and Build Settings), you can set:
* **App Name, Icon, & Launch Screen**
* **Minimum iOS Version & Device Support** (iPhone only, iPad, or Mac)
* **Background Modes**: Allow the app to keep running in the background for audio playback, GPS location tracking, VoIP calls, Bluetooth syncing, or background data fetching.
* **System Integrations (Capabilities)**: Push Notifications, Sign in with Apple, Apple Pay / Wallet, HealthKit, HomeKit, iCloud sync, Widgets, Live Activities (Dynamic Island), NFC tag reading, and Siri / App Intents.

---

### 4. What Your App *Cannot* Change (Blocked by Apple)
For privacy and security, third-party apps on the App Store **cannot**:
* Toggle system-wide Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Airplane Mode, or Cellular Data on/off.
* Grant themselves Camera, Location, or Microphone permissions without the user tapping "Allow".
* Change the user's system wallpaper, system-wide font, or other apps' settings.

---

Are you looking to control a specific setting in an app you're building? Tell me what you have in mind and we can set it up!

**Directly inside a standalone app: Correct, you cannot.** Apple blocks third-party apps from directly switching your active SIM/eSIM or changing which line handles Cellular Data (to prevent malicious apps from hijacking your connection or running up roaming charges).

**However, there is a big loophole using Apple’s Shortcuts system.**

While third-party apps are blocked, Apple’s built-in **Shortcuts** app has system-level privileges to control Dual SIM settings, including:
* **Switching which SIM uses Cellular Data**
* **Changing your Default Voice Line**
* **Turning a specific eSIM/SIM line On or Off**
* **Toggling 5G / LTE or Data Roaming per line**

---

### How We Can Actually Build This (The Workaround)

Even though a custom app can't flip the switch by itself, **a custom app can trigger a Shortcut that flips the switch.** 

Depending on what your goal is, you have two ways to do this:

#### Option 1: No-Code (Just a 1-Tap Button or Automation)
If you just want a fast way to switch carriers without digging through `Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data`:
1. Open the built-in **Shortcuts** app on your iPhone.
2. Create a shortcut using the **"Set Default Line"** action (you can set it to switch **Cellular Data** to SIM 1 or SIM 2).
3. Add that shortcut to your **Home Screen**, **Control Center**, **Lock Screen**, or **Action Button** for a 1-tap toggle—or set an **Automation** to switch SIMs automatically when you arrive at or leave a specific location (like work or home).

#### Option 2: A Custom App + Shortcut Hybrid
If you want **smart logic** that Shortcuts can't do on its own—for example:
* Testing ping/speed and alerting you when your current carrier is slow or dead,
* Tracking how much data you've used on each plan, or
* Providing a custom dashboard/widget to manage your lines,

We **can** build an iOS app that handles all the logic/UI and then calls `shortcuts://run-shortcut?name=SwitchToSIM2` to perform the actual carrier switch.

---
